_what_this_is: A ruling about WHERE a build input may live, and a register of the code that still breaks it. The gate derives from this file: src/gate_no_scratchpad_inputs.py.

RULING.rule: No script may take an input from a session scratchpad or from /tmp. Inputs live in dataset/build/ (a result), dataset/declarations/ (a ruling) or dataset/cache/ (a fetched page). Nowhere else.
RULING.why: A scratchpad path carries a session id. The id changes when the session restarts, and the directory does not survive a reboot or a move between machines. Code holding such a path is correct exactly once, on one machine, in one session, and silently wrong everywhere after.
RULING.the_instance_that_produced_this_ruling: bio_select.py read the Pro Football Archives claims from SCRATCH/nflverse/pfa-copy.json behind an os.path.exists guard. The archive moved to bghq-mac on 2026-09-07, the path died with the laptop session, the guard turned a missing 44 MB input into an empty dict, and every PFA fact left the bios without one word of complaint: 2,249 military-service claims, 4,232 death dates, 4,166 death places, plus high school, kin, height, weight and draft. gate_coach_runs R4 caught it only as a prose diff -- 'He was a United States Army veteran.' gone from Les Dodson -- never as 'an input is missing'. The identical claims were in build/pfa-pre1950.json, byte-for-byte, the entire time (sha256 5757efe2b2dc9b50051df2f8f51828d39d3205700e58294d4786bba8cde785fb).
RULING.the_guard_is_the_bug: os.path.exists(p) around a load-bearing read does not make the code robust, it makes the failure invisible. A required input that is absent must stop the run. bio_select.required() is the shape: resolve under BASE, raise SystemExit naming the file.
RULING.recovery: The laptop scratchpads were preserved at ~/Documents/session-scratch-from-laptop-2026-09-07/<session-id>/scratchpad/. Every path below except the four under literal /tmp can still be read from there. That folder is explicitly temporary and goes when the laptop's copy of the archive goes, so recovering a file means MOVING it into dataset/build/, not repointing at the preserved copy.

_how_to_close_one: Decide what the file is. If it is a RESULT, move it into dataset/build/ and read it from there. If it is a true INTERMEDIATE, the script that consumes it must also produce it, in the same run. Then delete the entry. An entry may not be deleted merely because the path was repointed at the preserved folder.

_open_question_for_ryan.media-guide-prose-census.json: measured,: Asked Yearbooks which census ingest_guide_prose should read; its session ended before answering, so I measured it. RESULT: all 20 guides I need are in build-reports/corpus-census.csv, joinable on filename -- its doc_id is the file stem ('bears-1985-media-guide-chicago-c'), which carries club and year in the same convention my mapping uses. So the census CAN serve the (club, year) -> file join; no club column is needed and the join I feared is not one. BUT it does not supersede the file: the census's classification columns are 'unread' for most post-1950 rows (Yearbooks read pre-1950 completely and post-1950 on a stated sample of 56 of 2,462), where classified4 carries measurements for all 1,880. RECOMMENDATION: keep build-reports/media-guide-prose-census.json. It is frozen, self-contained and gates cleanly, where the census is mid-build and its klass column is still filling in. Switching would couple a stable ingest to a moving file to save one artefact. Revisit if the census is ever finished and someone wants the duplicate gone -- the join is known to work.
